images.title: Patterns that come back
images.purpose: Show that day and night, and the school week, each repeat by a rule, so each is a pattern.
images.composition: Two horizontal strips stacked with wide space between them, each centred.
images.exact_structure: Top strip: 4 equal square boxes in a row, alternating a amber #E69F00 Sun circle, a teal #0072B2 Moon crescent, a amber #E69F00 Sun circle, a teal #0072B2 Moon crescent. Bottom strip: 7 equal square boxes in a row, the first 6 holding the days Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat and the seventh holding Mon again, outlined in reddish purple #CC79A7. All boxes the same size and evenly spaced. Exactly 2 strips, 4 boxes, 7 boxes.
labels: Mon to Sat, then Mon again
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a strip with a different number of boxes
images.takeaway: A pattern is something that comes back again and again by a rule.
images.description: A strip of Sun, Moon, Sun, Moon and a week strip from Mon to Sat that returns to Mon.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at where each strip starts to repeat and say the rule in their own words.

image_decisions.why: Day and night and the weekly timetable are one picture of repeating; the two strips carry it.
